:::{#thm-chain-rule-events}
#### Chain rule for several events

The probability that several [events](#def-event) all occur
is the probability of the first event,
times the [conditional probability](#def-conditional-prob) of each later event
given all the events before it.
For any events $A_1, \dots, A_n$ with $\Pr(A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_{n-1}) > 0$:

$$
\Pr(A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_n)
= \Pr(A_1) \prod_{i=2}^{n} \Pr(A_i \mid A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_{i-1})
$$

:::

::: proof

For $n = 2$, the statement is @thm-law-conditional-prob.
Suppose it holds for $n - 1$ events, and let $B = A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_{n-1}$.
Then $\Pr(B) > 0$, so @thm-law-conditional-prob applies to $A_n$ and $B$:

$$
\ba
\Pr(A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_n)
&= \Pr(A_n \cap B)
&& \text{(definition of } B \text{)}
\\ &= \Pr(A_n \mid B) \cd \Pr(B)
&& \text{(law of conditional probability)}
\ea
$$

Each set $A_1 \cap \dots \cap A_{i-1}$ with $i \le n - 1$ contains $B$,
so its probability is at least $\Pr(B) > 0$,
and the statement for $n - 1$ events expands $\Pr(B)$.

:::
